abstract: We study compatibility of planar layers around subgraphs whose one-edge completions have larger thickness. If two graphs meet exactly in two vertices, share one missing-edge endpoint, and both one-edge completions have thickness greater than $k$, then joining their two private missing endpoints also has thickness greater than $k$. The proof contracts prescribed-layer paths to temporary spokes and reembeds components at a cutvertex; no original spoke edges are required. For two $K_9$-minus-edge subgraphs the overlap bound is sharp: a supplied 15-vertex, 68-edge biplanar nine-chromatic certificate has three shared vertices. We then prove that, outside an actual $K_{10}-\{ab,cd\}$, no connected component of the common neighborhood of $a,b$ can contact both $c,d$. This excludes nontriangle common boundaries containing the opposite missing pair. For two common-triangle $K_9$-minus-edge subgraphs beside the same central host, we establish parallel-attachment orientation, bridge-layer transfer, and crossed-attachment exclusions for each of three connector roles. Except for an explicitly stated tight-edge corollary, these results need no Euler equality, degree bound, or criticality assumption. Complete hand proofs are accompanied by small standard-library path audits and a rotation-system checker for the positive control. The results strengthen the established linking framework without assuming minor closure of biplanarity. They do not classify all common-triangle attachments or establish a general nine-color bound; the Earth–Moon problem remains unresolved.

coauthors.contribution: Removed the unnecessary spoke-edge assumptions from the general two-shared-vertex theorem and independently audited the overlap, parallel-attachment and three connector proofs and supporting checks.

title: Two-vertex overlaps and layer constraints in biplanar graphs
